content: Borkum Riff is a renowned brand of pipe tobacco that originated in Denmark and is produced by Swedish Match. It is one of the most globally recognized pipe tobacco brands, having been introduced in 1968. During the Age of Discovery, Swedish explorers first arrived in North America in 1638, establishing a colony in Delaware. They began trading with the indigenous population, exchanging Swedish goods for local products such as furs. Among these local goods, tobacco stood out for its immense appeal in Europe. Recognizing this opportunity, Queen Kristina of Sweden commissioned skilled artisans to refine the production of high-quality pipe tobacco, catering to the European nobility. This tradition of excellence in pipe tobacco production has been carried forward by Borkum Riff, which has earned a distinguished reputation among pipe tobacco enthusiasts worldwide. The origins of the Borkum Riff brand can be traced back to the early 1960s when a pipe tobacco blend was introduced in Sweden under this name. Before this, Borkum Riff was known only as the name of a lighthouse located at 53° 58' N, 6° 22' E in the Helgoland Bay of the North Sea, off the Dutch coast. This lighthouse was a familiar landmark for sailors and was frequently mentioned in Swedish radio weather reports. The initial Borkum Riff tobacco blend was a rough-cut mixture of Virginia and Burley tobaccos. Although its sales were initially slow, the addition of a whiskey flavor significantly boosted its popularity. By the late 1960s, Borkum Riff had become the third most popular pipe tobacco brand in Sweden, following Greve Hamilton and Caravelle. In 1968, a pivotal moment in Borkum Riff's history occurred when the Swedish Tobacco Company developed a new pipe tobacco blend with unique smoking characteristics. This blend was soft, rich, and mellow, offering a smooth smoking experience without causing irritation to the mouth. It was easy to handle, stayed lit well, and provided a light yet robust flavor with a pleasant aroma. This blend was particularly appealing to individuals transitioning from cigarette smoking to pipe smoking, and it quickly gained worldwide acclaim. The packaging of Borkum Riff was designed to reflect its premium quality. The pouch design, already established in the Swedish market, was chosen for its timeless simplicity and distinctive elements. The ship depicted on the packaging was inspired by a 17th-century engraving by Johann Baptista Homann, a German cartographer and engraver. The new blend was developed with the United States, the world's largest pipe tobacco market, in mind. In 1969, Borkum Riff's Bourbon Whiskey blend was introduced in the U.S., where it achieved remarkable success. The product received enthusiastic feedback from wholesalers, retailers, and consumers alike, with many claiming it was the pipe tobacco they had long desired. Over time, Borkum Riff expanded its presence to other markets, including Canada, Australia, Switzerland, Spain, New Zealand, Japan, France, Italy, and Germany, among others. Despite its global reach, the United States remains Borkum Riff's largest market.
